That means their economy will not be able to move forward until the conditions that are in the national interest of the United States and the interests of the Venezuelan people are met.", "reason": "What are the economic effects of a US oil quarantine on Venezuela's economy and oil sector?"},{"unit_ids": ["D921563fa23.P009.S006", "D921563fa23.P009.S007", "D921563fa23.P009.S008"], "anchor": null, "reason": "How effective are targeted oil-vessel seizures under court orders as economic leverage to change a sanctioned country's governance?"},{"unit_ids": ["D921563fa23.P027.S003", "D921563fa23.P027.S004", "D921563fa23.P027.S005"], "anchor": null, "reason": "What are the costs and effectiveness of continuing oil sanctions enforcement until governance changes occur?"},{"unit_ids": ["D921563fa23.P031.S001"], "anchor": "The way to address it to the benefit of the Venezuelan people is to get private companies that are not from Iran or somewhere else to go in, invest in the equipment that hasn't been invested in in 20 years because none of the profits that have been made from the oil have been reinvested – it's all been stolen – and that's going to take outside companies that come in and know how to do that.", "reason": "What are the economic gains from allowing Western private companies to invest in Venezuela's oil sector?"},{"unit_ids": ["D921563fa23.P034.S001"], "anchor": "that will spin off tremendous royalties for the people of Venezuela to benefit the people of that country, not the handful of people at the top but the people.", "reason": "How does shifting oil revenue distribution from elites to royalties affect Venezuelan welfare outcomes?"}]}
